title: Building Analytics Excellence
text:
Open-source tools and frameworks developed to solve real-world analytics challenges:



PAGfxns - The Predictive Analytics Group's functions (PAGfxns) package is focused on feature engineering package for enrollment predictive modeling. Transforms applicant data into temporal behavior derivatives used in prediction models. It is designed to be application-platform agnostic. Powering the enrollment predictions for 50,000+ applicants for the Fall 2026 incoming class. In-house application - approach transferable to similar use cases.
GELI - The Geographical-Endpoint Landscape Index (GELI) package leverages the concept that entities with similar features should behave in the same manner. GELI identifies regions following and diverging from this principle. Developed to serve the demands of MSU's Office of Admissions, GELI now possess screening and search capabilities as it enters its second year of application. In-house application - approach transferable to similar use cases.
theHUB - The Haabefuld Utility Box (theHUB), is a comprehensive analytics toolkit for higher education institutions, featuring functions, scripts, and worked examples for student success analysis. Initially developed for Michigan State University, it is a collection of analysis tools composed of functions, scripts, electronic notebooks, and worked examples. theHUB was designed to share these tools with the MSU community to improve the analyses of student outcomes, student success, and survey responses.





RaeveStoberi - The RaeveStoberi package is our in-house application for harvesting, extracting, and cleaning sports-related data. RaeveStoberi currently serves our need for constructing player, team, game, play-by-play, and league datasets for the NHL, WNBA, Unrivaled Basketball League, and various NCAA sports. In-house application - constantly expanding to support new sports projects.





MSUthemes - The MSUthemes package provides colour palettes and themes for Michigan State University (MSU) and comprehensive colour support for all Big Ten Conference institutions. The package includes MSU-specific palettes (sequential, diverging, and qualitative) designed to align with MSU's branding guidelines, uses the Metropolis font (MSU's chosen font) in the construction of the plots, as well as the primary and secondary colour palettes for all 18 Big Ten institutions, making it ideal for multi-institutional comparisons and collaborative research visualizations using ggplot2.






Sports Analytics: [Brief project descriptions] 
Higher Education: Drawing on economics, analytics, and predictive modelling, PAG provides a unique perspective on student-centric quandaries. We actively develop deposit and cancellation likelihood models for the incoming class along with recommending recruiting communities for future incoming classes. Using rigorour, evidence-based methods we have developed sound deposit likelihood models that are able to identify ~80% of applicants who deposit in the preceeding January, four months before the deposit deadline.

section: From Complex Data to Clear Direction
text:
From Complex Data to Clear Direction
I believe that the intersection of analytics and leadership creates transformational opportunities in sports and higher education. With over 15 years of experience building analytics programs and leading data-driven initiatives, I help organizations see beyond the numbers to make confident, strategic decisions.
My approach combines rigorous statistical analysis with a deep understanding of organizational culture. Whether optimizing roster decisions for sports teams or predicting student success in higher education, I focus on building sustainable analytics capabilities that empower teams at every level.
Currently, I lead the Predictive Analytics Group at Michigan State University's Enrollment Services, where I've developed evidence-based methods that improved the Office of Admissions' ability to identify high-likelihood of enrollment communities for recruitment and identified in January approximately 80% of the admitted applicants who are likely to enroll. I also teach in MSU's Sports Analytics Graduate Certificate program, guiding the next generation of analytics leaders through real-world applications.
I'm passionate about partnering with organizations ready to transform their approach to data—whether through strategic consulting engagements or by joining teams committed to building truly data-driven cultures.

The Journey
My path to analytics leadership began in scientific research, where I learned the rigor of data-driven discovery. Since founding exeResearch in 2008, I've applied these principles across industries, ultimately finding my calling at the intersection of sports, education, and analytics.

title: Onboarding
section: Building High-Performance Analytics Teams: A Proven Onboarding Framework
text:
Building High-Performance Analytics Teams: A Proven Onboarding Framework
One of my core leadership philosophies is that exceptional analytics outcomes begin with exceptional team foundations. This framework, which I’ve developed and refined through years of leading analytics teams, ensures new team members are positioned for success from day one.

The Strategic Value of Structured Onboarding
In analytics organizations – whether in sports, higher education, or other data-driven environments – the first 30 days often determine whether a talented analyst becomes a high-impact contributor or struggles to find their footing. This framework transforms onboarding from an administrative checklist into a strategic opportunity for building a culture.


Pre-Arrival Foundation (2 Weeks Before Start)

Communication & Expectation Setting

Stakeholder notifications across the analytics ecosystem
HR coordination for seamless administrative integration
Technology access provisioning (systems, repositories, collaborative platforms)
“How I Like to be Mentored” assessment to personalize support
Strategic one-on-one scheduling with key team members
Onboarding Partner selection and preparation



Creating Connection Before Day One

Welcome package curation (team swag, local gift cards, professional tools)
Early delivery to build excitement and belonging




Week One: Integration & Immersion

Day One: First Impressions Matter

Structured morning introductions
Team lunch to build informal connections
Technical onboarding (shared repositories, project access, documentation)



Daily Touchpoints

Brief check-ins to address questions in real-time
Gradual introduction to team workflows and standards



Week One Conclusion

Formal Onboarding Partner introduction with clear expectations
Comprehensive week-end review to calibrate next steps




Sustained Support: Weeks 2-4

Bi-directional Feedback Loops

Regular check-ins with both the new member and the Colleague Connector
Proactive identification of learning opportunities
Adjustment of support based on individual needs



30-Day Milestone

Comprehensive review addressing questions, concerns, and growth opportunities
Transition planning from structured support to organic integration




Outcomes This Framework Delivers

For Team Members:

Higher job satisfaction and retention rates
Clearer understanding of success metrics



For Organizations:

Consistent culture transmission
Reduced manager time investment after initial setup
Scalable approach for growing analytics teams



For Leaders:

Systematic approach that frees time for strategic work
Clear documentation for delegation and succession planning
Demonstration of investment in team development




Adaptability Across Contexts
This framework’s strength lies in its flexibility. I’ve successfully adapted it for:

Remote-first analytics teams
Hybrid university research groups
Fast-paced sports analytics environments
Cross-functional data science initiatives

The principles remain constant: intentional connection, systematic support, and clear communication create the foundation for analytics excellence.

title: CLAUDE.md
text:
This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.


This is a Quarto-based website for exeResearch, a sports analytics and data science consultancy founded by Emilio Xavier Esposito. The site showcases services in sports decision analytics, leadership & management consulting, data-driven enrollment strategies, and applied data science. The website includes a blog called “The Model Scout” with posts on sports analytics, leadership, and data projects.





quarto preview
This starts a local development server with live reload.



quarto render
This builds the static site to the _site/ directory.



quarto render index.qmd
quarto render posts/shot-selection/index.qmd



quarto render --no-cache







_quarto.yml: Main configuration file defining site metadata, navigation, and theme settings

Uses dual theme: flatly (light) and darkly (dark) with user color scheme preference
Navbar configured with right-aligned links to blog, about, and social profiles
Page layout set to full with table of contents disabled site-wide

index.qmd: Homepage featuring hero section and content sections for services, projects, about, team, and contact

Uses custom CSS classes (.hero-section, .content-section, .alt-bg, etc.)
Internal navigation via anchor links to section IDs

blog.qmd: Blog listing page using Quarto’s listing feature

Configured to display posts from posts/ directory
Sorted by date descending with RSS feed enabled
Shows: date, title, author, categories, description

about.qmd: About page using Jolla template with social links





Each blog post lives in posts/<post-name>/index.qmd
posts/_metadata.yml: Default settings for all blog posts

freeze: true - Computational output is frozen (cached) to avoid re-running code
title-block-banner: true - Posts use banner-style title blocks






styles.css: Custom CSS for the entire site

Hero section with full-viewport background image and gradient overlay
Alternating section backgrounds using .alt-bg class
Responsive grid layouts (.project-grid, .service-areas)
Mobile breakpoint at 768px





Posts can include R code chunks (or Python) that execute during rendering. The freeze feature in posts/_metadata.yml caches computational results to speed up subsequent builds. When code needs to re-execute, use quarto render --no-cache or delete specific freeze cache in .quarto/_freeze/.



The rendered site goes to _site/ by default. The commented line # output-dir: docs in _quarto.yml suggests GitHub Pages deployment was considered but is currently disabled.






New blog posts should be created in posts/<post-slug>/index.qmd with YAML frontmatter:
---
title: "Post Title"
author: "Author Name"
date: "YYYY-MM-DD"
categories: [category1, category2]
description: "Brief description for listings"
image: "thumbnail.jpg"  # optional
---



Based on existing posts: sports analytics, basketball, R, and related analytics topics.





_quarto.yml - Site configuration and navigation
index.qmd - Homepage with all main sections
blog.qmd - Blog listing page
posts/_metadata.yml - Default post settings
styles.css - Custom styling
